citation.authors: Mengozzi A, Biancalana E, Parolini F, Baldi S, Raggi F, Solini A
citation.title: Normal Versus Slowly Processed Pasta and Post-Prandial Glucose Homeostasis in Healthy Subjects: A Pilot Study

population.description: Fourteen healthy male volunteers from Pisa University Hospital personnel; inclusion age 18-60 y, BMI 18.5-25.0 kg/m2, normal fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c; no acute complications, chronic comorbidity or drugs. Age 31 ± 9 y and BMI 21.3 ± 1.9 kg/m2 (Results 3.1, Table 1; mean ± SD per Methods 2.6). Randomized crossover, both meals in all 14.

protocols.name: screening_fasted
protocols.description: Screening-visit blood draw (Methods 2.1; Table 1, row Fasting plasma glucose); the paper does not say at what hour or after how long a fast it was drawn, so a morning after a 10 h overnight fast is assumed; no meal; 30-minute run-in stands for the single sample

findings.description: Fasting plasma glucose at the screening visit, all 14 men (Table 1)

location.where: Table 1, column Baseline (n = 14), row Fasting plasma glucose (mmol∙L−1); mean ± standard deviation per Methods 2.6

left_out.what: all of Table 2 (fasting, 2-h and iAUC of glucose, insulin, GIP and GLP-1, NP and SP): Methods 2.6 labels every ± as SD, but the paper's own numbers contradict it (the study-day fasting glucose spread is a sixth of the screening spread in Table 1 in the same 14 men, and the NP-SP 2-h insulin difference printed 'ns' would be significant as SDs at any within-person correlation); the kind of uncertainty cannot be established, and is not relabelled by inference

post-meal values of both mixed-meal tests (Table 2 2-h values and iAUCs, Figure 1): the meal's 10 g olive oil and 10 g parmesan have no composition printed (Methods 2.3, 2.4 give only the pasta's), so its fat and protein grams cannot be written
2-h plasma glucose, NP and SP (Table 2): unit printed as mmol∙min∙L−1, an area unit for a concentration
plasma glucose iAUC, NP and SP (Table 2): unit printed as mmol∙L−1, with no time unit
absolute insulin peak, NP and SP (Results 3.2): no uncertainty printed
glucose, insulin, GIP and GLP-1 time courses 0-180 min after the meal, NP and SP (Figure 1 only); also the 30-min glucose peak difference described in Results 3.2
screening total, LDL and HDL cholesterol (Table 1)
